title: Hidden joy
hookLine: no soul knows what joy is kept hidden for them (32:17)

cards: A box handed over with a grin, and the giver says: don't shake it. Half the joy is not knowing. The other half is finding, when you open it, that the giver knew you better than you thought.
As-Sajdah has just described people getting up in the dark to pray, unseen. The very next verse says what's waiting for them. Or rather, it says something more interesting: that nobody knows.

teach.h: QURRAT A'YUN: COOLNESS OF THE EYES.
teach.b: Pickthall: "No soul knoweth what is kept hid for them of joy, as a reward for what they used to do." The phrase Pickthall translates joy is qurrat a'yun, literally coolness of the eyes, an old Arabic idiom.

In a hot land, coolness is relief, and an old explanation in the dictionaries says tears of grief are hot, tears of happiness cool. So qurrat 'ayn is what cools your eyes, what makes you deeply, quietly glad.
The same idiom appears elsewhere in the Qur'an for spouses and children, and for the baby Musa.
Here it's kept hidden: ukhfiya, concealed. A hadith in Bukhari brings the verse to life.

teach.h: NO EYE HAS SEEN, NO EAR HAS HEARD.
teach.b: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said that God says: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has never occurred to any human heart.
Abu Hurayra, who reported it, added: recite if you wish, no soul knows what is kept hidden for them. Some early commentators noticed a symmetry.

teach.h: A HIDDEN DEED, A HIDDEN JOY.
teach.b: The people in the verse before prayed in secret, at night, where no one could see, so their reward is secret too: a hidden deed, answered with a hidden joy. A kind of justice, and a kind of tenderness.
The Qur'an gives many pictures of paradise: gardens, rivers, shade, fruit. Read with the hadith, this verse says those pictures fall short: whatever a person imagines, the reward is beyond it.
A hope never described, only promised, and kept hidden like the prayer that earned it.

how: Many Muslims value hidden good deeds, such as secret charity and night prayer, and recite 32:17 alongside the hadith of what no eye has seen when speaking of paradise.

games.q: you did something good, quietly, and no one saw. you're tempted to mention it. what does the verse's pairing suggest?
o: keep it hidden; a hidden deed, a hidden joy.
do it again in public next time.
games.why: some early commentators read 32:17 this way: those who prayed unseen are given a joy kept hidden.

practice: Think of one good thing you could do that nobody would ever know was you: paying for someone's coffee and slipping away, an anonymous kind note, a gift to a cause you tell no one about, fixing something at home before anyone sees it's broken.
Picture doing it, and keeping it to yourself afterward, even when you're tempted to mention it. If you pray, you can offer it quietly.

wordCard.voice: Hidden joy. Qurrat a'yun, the coolness of the eyes, which As-Sajdah says is kept hidden for those who prayed unseen. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: coolness of the eyes, the idiom for joy in 32:17.
